title: WORD MELT
goal: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

steps.action: Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
Stop there and look around the room.
Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

win: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.
supports: Exhale after “Return Seen”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Say Gently” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Charged → Say Gently → Listen Moment → Stop Room → Return Seen
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this with slurs, trauma phrases, voices, or material that escalates symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE INCH BEYOND EASY
goal: Competence grows at the edge, not at the cliff.

steps.action: Select a task you can already do.
Increase one dimension slightly: duration, complexity, independence, or visibility.
Complete that version and note what skill carried you through.
The next challenge must be earned by evidence, not demanded by shame.

win: ✓ Made the next challenge earn its place with evidence.
supports: Exhale after “Raise One Inch”; release extra blame.
I can use “Increase” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Select Task → Increase → Complete Version → Raise One Inch
safety:
PAUSE
Step back when challenge impairs recovery, safety, or essential functioning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.

steps.action: Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

win: ✓ I stated that honestly without making a false promise.
supports: Exhale after “Set Reopen”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Choose Size” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Read Bandwidth → Choose Size → Send Signal → Set Reopen
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use bandwidth limits to conceal immediate danger, threats, abuse, medical urgency, or information another person needs for safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THEN / NOW SUBTITLES
goal: Flashbacks need temporal translation.

steps.action: When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference.
Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair.
The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location.

win: ✓ Gave the replay a date and location instead of letting it become now.
supports: Gently exhale after “Date Location”; orient to now.
I can use “Include Age” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Alternate Lines → Include Age → Keep Eyes → Date Location
safety:
PAUSE
Contact emergency or trauma support if sense of where you are does not return.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT
goal: Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.

steps.action: Spot one part of the present condition that is really adequate: shelter, breath, effort, support, knowledge, or time for the next step.
Receive that adequacy without claiming everything is fine.
From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.

win: ✓ I found one thing that was already enough, then chose from there.
supports: Gently exhale after “Choose Non”; no forcing.
I can use “Receive Adequacy” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Identify Part → Receive Adequacy → Choose Non
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use contentment to minimise unmet needs or structural harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
goal: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

steps.action: Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

win: ✓ Noticed which emotion moved and which stayed.
supports: Exhale after “Tag Driver”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Hold Scene” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Pair → Hold Scene → Swap Variable → Tag Driver
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use imagined substitutions to rewrite trauma, deny facts, or continue once the scene becomes overwhelming or unreal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT IS NEW THIS LAP?
goal: Reflection ends when the loop stops producing data.

steps.action: At the start of another mental cycle, state the new fact, distinction, or decision it could add.
If nothing specific appears, name the lap ‘repetition’ and leave one written summary behind.
Move to a sensory or practical task.

win: ✓ The loop no longer needs one more answer.
supports: Exhale after “Move Sensory”; end the lap.
I can use “Name Lap” without another lap.
formula_flow: Find Novelty → Name Lap → Move Sensory
safety:
PAUSE
Return when new evidence actually arrives, not merely because discomfort returns.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY
goal: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

steps.action: Place two chairs apart.
Speak from your position using first person.
Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.

win: ✓ The next sentence can carry the boundary without carrying the fight.
supports: Exhale after “Return To Facts”; soften the jaw.
“Place Chairs” to “Return To Facts”: what loosened?
I can use “Speak Position” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Place Chairs → Speak Position → Switch Chair → Return To Facts
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this alone for traumatic relationships or if role-switching feels disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
goal: Disclosure should increase clarity, not steal control.

steps.action: Choose a trustworthy listener and agree on time, confidentiality, and a stop signal.
Share facts first, then feelings and meaning in manageable detail.
Pause to orient between sections.
End with what support you want now—not what the listener guesses.

win: ✓ I told enough truth to gain clarity without giving away control.
supports: Exhale after “End Support”; loosen the label.
I can use “Share” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Choose Trustworthy → Share → Pause Orient → End Support
safety:
PAUSE
Stop when speech becomes flooding, detached, pressured, or unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.

steps.action: Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
Give the prediction a real time window.
Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

win: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
supports: Exhale after “Update Odds”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Set Clock” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds
safety:
PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GROUNDING ANCHOR RELAY
goal: Rotate before one cue becomes background noise.

steps.action: Select four anchors from different systems: visual line, distant sound, contact pressure, joint position.
Spend a short interval with each and switch before getting used to it empties it.
Finish on the channel that restored the clearest present contact.

win: ✓ One channel brought the present back into focus.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Channel”; notice the room.
I can use “Switch Getting” to return here.
formula_flow: Select Different → Switch Getting → Finish Channel
safety:
PAUSE
Use fewer anchors if switching itself increases overload.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FEELING UNDER THE FEELING ABOUT IT
goal: Secondary emotion may be wearing the crown.

steps.action: Spot the primary emotion and its trigger.
Then finish: ‘About feeling this, I feel…’ Locate each in a different body area or colour.
Offer the primary state what it needs before addressing shame, anger, or fear about having it.

win: ✓ The first feeling finally got care before the second one took over.
supports: Exhale after “State Needs”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Finish About” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Emotion → Finish About → State Needs
safety:
PAUSE
Seek help if peeling exposes overwhelming trauma or self-attack.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: HALF-SPEED THE FIRST MOVE
goal: Slow the first move enough to catch the launch.

steps.action: Catch the first movement linked to the urge—turning, reaching, standing, typing.
do only that movement at half speed while observing its direction and tension.
Pause at completion and decide whether the second movement serves you.

win: ✓ Slowing the launch exposed the choice before the second move fired.
supports: Exhale after “Pause Completion”; mark the pause.
I can use “Observe Direction” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Identify Earliest → Observe Direction → Pause Completion
safety:
PAUSE
Do not slow a movement needed for immediate safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

steps.action: Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

win: ✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.
supports: Exhale after “Check Panel”; then keep moving.
I can use “Pick Smallest” before motivation.
formula_flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel
safety:
PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BLANK THE NAMEPLATE
goal: Cover the label and see what you choose without it.

steps.action: Picture the identity label on a removable card and turn it face down.
For the next decision, refer only to capacities, needs, facts, and values.
Choose.
Then uncover the label and compare what it would have predicted.

win: ✓ The label went dark. The choice still appeared.
supports: Exhale after “Uncover Name”; loosen the label.
I can use “Decision” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Picture Identity → Decision → Choose Shift → Uncover Name
safety:
PAUSE
Do not remove labels needed to communicate access, care, or safety needs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
goal: Ongoing sense can be sensed before the life story is consulted.

steps.action: For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.

win: ✓ For one minute, existence did not need a biography.
supports: Exhale after “End Reclaim”; loosen the label.
I can use “Stay Changing” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Don't Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if life-story quiet creates feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
goal: What someone did is not your identity property.

steps.action: Imagine three boxes: THEIR BEHAVIOUR; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.
Keep each thought in the right box.
Forgiveness is not required on command.
Take one action from the third box.

win: ✓ The surge has a shape now instead of filling everything.
supports: Gently exhale after “Act From Choice”; no breath-holding.
Look back: “Imagine Three Boxes” → “Act From Choice”.
I can use “Keep Each Part” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Imagine Three Boxes → Keep Each Part → Skip Forced Forgiveness → Act From Choice
safety:
PAUSE
Use support when blame, shame, or safety concerns remain intense.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MEMORY REVIEW BY APPOINTMENT ONLY
goal: Choose when to revisit a memory instead of replaying it all day.

steps.action: Set a limited review window and catch the reason for revisiting.
When replay appears outside it, add one keyword to the Notice and redirect to present activity.
At the appointment, process purposefully or cancel if no useful aim remains.

win: ✓ The memory got an appointment instead of the whole day.
supports: Exhale after “Remain Appointment”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Add Keyword” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Set Limited → Add Keyword → Remain Appointment
safety:
PAUSE
Intrusive trauma memories may need treatment rather than scheduling alone.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MATCH THE TASK TO THE BODY’S TEMPERATURE
goal: Action fails when stimulation and state are badly paired.

steps.action: Read current body alarm as lower, middle, or high.
Select work with matching demand: energising movement for low, steady production for medium, simple contained tasks for high.
Reassess after one unit and change lanes if needed.

win: ✓ I matched the task to the body I actually had today.
supports: I can use “Select Work” before motivation.
formula_flow: Read Body → Select Work → Reassess
safety:
PAUSE
Do not treat serious fatigue or agitation as a productivity puzzle.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS
goal: Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.

steps.action: Name the task’s essential purpose.
Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.

win: ✓ I built the smallest version that still counted, finished it, and left upgrades optional.
supports: Exhale after “Build Smallest”; release the score.
I can use “Remove Feature” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Name Task → Remove Feature → Build Smallest
safety:
PAUSE
Maintain full standards for safety-critical, clinical, legal, or hard to undo work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAY THE PROCESS IMMEDIATELY
goal: Delayed outcomes train weakly; immediate feedback can bridge the gap.

steps.action: Choose a small healthy reward delivered right after the process action, regardless of final result: music, a short break, a pleasant drink, or a brief message.
Name exactly which behaviour earns the reward and keep the reward proportionate.

win: ✓ Behaviour got paid now, not someday.
supports: Exhale after “Name the Reward”; release extra blame.
I can use “Name the Reward” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Choose Small → Name the Reward
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid rewards that undermine the goal or create financial, food, or substance problems.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
goal: A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.

steps.action: Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.

win: ✓ My part is clearer, and the rest is not mine to carry.
supports: Exhale after “Hold Setting”; release extra load.
I can use “Pick Door” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Name Contact → Pick Door → Lower One → Hold Setting
safety:
PAUSE
If there is abuse, stalking, coercion, violence, or immediate danger, prioritise safety planning and professional support over gradual access changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TAKE UP 5% MORE SPACE
goal: Social threat often folds the body before any decision is made.

steps.action: Widen feet, elbows, chest, or seating position by a small manageable amount.
Keep the change below performance or dominance.
Observe what the expanded shape signals internally and which words become easier to access.

win: ✓ Five percent more space unlocked words that threat posture was hiding.
supports: Gently exhale after “Observe Shape”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Keep Change” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Widen Feet → Keep Change → Observe Shape
safety:
PAUSE
Stay compact when wider posture would make the situation less safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SETTLE WITHOUT USING BREATH
goal: When respiration is a trigger, use other doors.

steps.action: Choose pressure from a surface, steady gaze, mild temperature, and slow movement.
Sequence them without checking breathing.
Notice which channel restores the clearest orientation to your current setting and keep only that one for the final interval.

win: ✓ I found a settling door that did not require touching the breath.
supports: Gently exhale after “Choose the Channel”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Check Sequence” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Choose Pressure → Check Sequence → Choose the Channel
safety:
PAUSE
Use medical care for breathing symptoms rather than on purpose ignoring them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: UNWIND IN REVERSE
goal: Release the body by retracing its body alarm order backward.

steps.action: Recall which muscle group tightened last.
Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.

win: ✓ Retracing the alarm backward taught the body how to unwind forward.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Original”; mark the pause.
I can use “Soften Work” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Recall Muscle → Soften Work → Pause Handoff → Finish Original
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid manipulating painful, injured, or medically affected areas.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHICH WAY DOES THE URGE POINT?
goal: Body alarm becomes clearer when given a vector.

steps.action: Without acting, classify the bodily impulse as toward, away, against, downward, upward, or still.
Notice the body region carrying the arrow.
Ask what safe action could honour the information without blindly completing the vector.

win: ✓ The urge found a direction without becoming an order.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Safe”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Body” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Act Classify → Body → Ask Safe
safety:
PAUSE
Create distance and support if the vector involves violence or self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND FIVE COLOURS WITHOUT CHASING THEM
goal: Threat scanning narrows the palette.

steps.action: Keep your body still enough for safety and locate five distinct colours across the scene.
Name shade and location, not emotional meaning.
Do not move toward pleasant colours or away from unpleasant ones.
Finish with the colour farthest from the trigger.

win: ✓ Five colours pulled attention out of the chase and back into the scene.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Colour”; notice the room.
I can use “Name Shade” to return here.
formula_flow: Keep Body → Name Shade → Don't Move → Finish Colour
safety:
PAUSE
Maintain hazard awareness in public or moving environments.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET ONE TASTE FINISH
goal: Consumption slows when flavour is followed to zero.

steps.action: Take one small bite or sip.
Track taste from first contact through peak, transformation, and complete disappearance.
Do not add another until the original flavour has ended.
Notice the exact point where wanting separates from tasting.

win: ✓ The taste ended; wanting did not have to chase it.
supports: One exhale after “Watch Wanting”; redirect attention.
I can use “Track Taste” amid noise.
formula_flow: Take Small → Track Taste → Don't Add → Watch Wanting
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use for restrictive eating or where clinical nutrition guidance differs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.

steps.action: Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain.
For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything.
Choose the one object whose real function supports what you can do now, then use only that function.

win: ✓ The room went back to having jobs instead of demands.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Helper”; release extra blame.
I can use “Name Jobs” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Scan Objects → Name Jobs → Drop Demands → Choose Helper
safety:
PAUSE
Stop for visual pain, dizziness, nausea, disorientation, compulsive scanning, or any real emergency requiring immediate action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: QUARANTINE THE UNAVAILABLE VARIABLE
goal: Analysis cannot solve what depends on a condition that does not exist.

steps.action: Name the exact variable outside present control—another person’s decision, test result, future opening, missing resource.
State what change would make processing useful.
Until then, store the problem with that trigger and refuse further computation.

win: ✓ I quarantined the variable that does not exist yet and stopped computing it.
supports: Exhale after “Store It Away”; mark the pause.
I can use “State Change” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Name Variable → State Change → Store It Away
safety:
PAUSE
Continue any preparation that remains possible while the variable is unavailable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ISSUE THE DECISION RECEIPT
goal: Completed choices need proof of closure.

steps.action: Picture the decision, main reason, date, one simple action, review date, and conditions that justify reopening.
Sign it.
When doubt returns, compare it with the reopening conditions rather than relitigating emotion.

win: ✓ The decision now has a receipt, so doubt needs evidence to reopen it.
supports: Exhale after “Return Reopening”; mark the pause.
formula_flow: Picture Decision → Sign → Return Reopening
safety:
PAUSE
Reopen immediately when material safety or ethical information changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: Recurring concerns keep roaming when no destination exists.

steps.action: Assign the concern to one place: a named person, calendar slot, document, task name, or deliberate release.
Say the address in your mind and route the thought there each time it returns.
If no useful address exists, mark the thought UNDELIVERABLE and let it pass without rerouting.

win: ✓ No useful address. That thought can stop roaming.
supports: Exhale after “Mark Undeliverable”; mark the pause.
I can use “Route Address” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Assign Concern → Route Address → Mark Undeliverable
safety:
PAUSE
Do not redirect warning thoughts that require immediate evaluation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE PROMISE AT THE CROSSROADS
goal: A private intention is weakest where renegotiation begins.

steps.action: Spot the exact decision moment and place a visible or mental commitment there: a door cue, calendar alert, prepared object, or agreed reminder.
Make the cue name the exact action, not a motivational slogan.
When that decision point arrives, follow the cue before renegotiation begins.

win: ✓ I put the promise exactly where renegotiation usually starts.
supports: Exhale after “Meet the Crossroads”; release extra blame.
I can use “State Action” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Identify Decision → State Action
safety:
PAUSE
Respect privacy and avoid public commitments that create shame or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.

steps.action: Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

win: ✓ One work pulse found the gear motivation could only guess at.
supports: Exhale after “Set Gear”; release extra blame.
I can use “Full Stop” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear
safety:
PAUSE
Stop for pain, illness, exhaustion, agitation, compulsive timing, or any task where interruptions create safety risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: HARVEST THE PROOF OF PROGRESS
goal: Gains must be stored before motivation can spend them.

steps.action: Collect three concrete differences created by prior effort—speed, quality, recovery time, knowledge, frequency, distance.
Attach dates or examples.
Select the one doable step that becomes reasonable because one difference now exists.

win: ✓ Progress became stored evidence instead of a feeling I could forget.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Action”; release extra blame.
I can use “Date Examples” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Create Prior → Date Examples → Choose Action
safety:
PAUSE
Do not cherry-pick progress to ignore deteriorating health or strategy.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN PURPOSE INTO A TUESDAY
goal: Meaning needs a recurring appointment.

steps.action: Picture the larger purpose, then spot one weekly behaviour that materially expresses it.
Choose day, cue, duration, and minimum version.
Remove inspirational language until the procedure can survive an ordinary Tuesday.

win: ✓ I turned purpose into something ordinary enough to survive Tuesday.
supports: Gently exhale after “Remove Inspirational”; orient to now.
I can use “Choose Day” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Picture Larger → Choose Day → Remove Inspirational
safety:
PAUSE
Revise the procedure when it no longer serves the purpose.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
goal: Several clues can be one echo wearing different clothes.

steps.action: Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.

win: ✓ Five clues stopped pretending to be five independent witnesses.
supports: Exhale after “Recheck Claim”; watch the thought.
I can use “Link Sources” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Name Clues → Link Sources → Collapse Copies → Recheck Claim
safety:
PAUSE
Do not collapse separate danger signs or ignore qualified medical, legal, financial, or safety evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHOOSE WITH THE UNKNOWN INCLUDED
goal: Completeness is not always available before action expires.

steps.action: Name the unknowns, notice which could change the decision, and compare available evidence with your preselected threshold.
Once the evidence line is reached, choose while naming what remains uncertain.
Build a review point for the critical unknowns.

win: ✓ The unknown stayed in the room without taking over the steering.
supports: Exhale after “Build Review”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Choose Uncertain” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Change → Choose Uncertain → Build Review
safety:
PAUSE
Raise the threshold when error would be hard to undo or dangerous.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE LOCAL REASON
goal: Global meaning may be unavailable; today’s significance can still exist.

steps.action: Search only within the next twenty-four hours for one person, place, promise, task, or act that matters.
Name why it matters locally.
Give it ten minutes of undivided behaviour.

win: ✓ Feeling and fact took separate seats. The room got bigger.
supports: Exhale after “Invest Time”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Name Reason” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Find Anchor → Name Reason → Invest Time
safety:
PAUSE
Seek urgent help if meaninglessness includes suicidal thinking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
goal: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.

steps.action: State clearly what was wrong or unwanted.
Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial.
Let the value belong to you, not to the harm.

win: ✓ The load shrank to the piece that truly belongs here.
supports: Exhale after “Let Value”; release extra load.
I can use “Name Boundary” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: State Clearly → Name Boundary → Let Value
safety:
PAUSE
Do not force lessons before grief or shock has space.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
goal: Finite life can expose counterfeit urgency.

steps.action: Imagine looking back from life’s end—not to frighten yourself, but to rank.
Which current demand disappears?
Which relationship, integrity choice, health need, or contribution remains?
Give the surviving priority one concrete slot today.

win: ✓ Counterfeit urgency failed the last-day test; one real priority survived.
supports: Exhale after “Give Surviving”; slow the clock.
formula_flow: Imagine Back → Demand → Remain Relationship → Give Surviving
safety:
PAUSE
Skip mortality reflection when it intensifies anxiety, grief, or self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAIN IS PRESENT; LIFE HAS OTHER DEPARTMENTS
goal: Suffering should not absorb the entire identity budget.

steps.action: Say exactly what is hurting.
Then name three processes continuing alongside it: caring, learning, digesting, noticing, working, resting, relating.
Choose one small action from a continuing department without denying the pain.

win: ✓ Pain stayed real, and another department of life stayed open.
supports: Gently exhale after “Choose Small”; orient to now.
I can use “Continue Alongside” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Describe Hurting → Continue Alongside → Choose Small
safety:
PAUSE
Obtain care when pain or distress needs direct treatment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE BIG QUESTION A ROOM, NOT THE HOUSE
goal: Existential inquiry needs boundaries to coexist with living.

steps.action: Choose a short time for the big question.
think about one clear question and stop when the time ends. You do not require a final answer.
Then do one normal task that shows how you want to live now.

win: ✓ The big question got a room; the rest of life kept the house.
supports: Exhale after “Return To Life”; watch the thought.
“Bring One Question” proves thought is observable.
“Set the Room” versus “Return To Life”: what eased?
I can use “Bring One Question” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Set the Room → Bring One Question → Return To Life
safety:
PAUSE
Seek mental health support when existential repetitive thinking impairs safety or functioning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
goal: Research may be serving emotional certainty, not information.

steps.action: Finish this sentence: ‘If I keep checking, I hope to guarantee that…’ Ask whether any amount of data can provide that emotional promise.
Gather only information that changes action; treat the remaining demand as uncertainty to carry.

win: ✓ Useful information ended where the guarantee-seeking began.
supports: Exhale after “Remain Demand”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Remain Demand” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Finish Sentence → Remain Demand
safety:
PAUSE
Do not stop investigation while essential facts are still obtainable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHERE EXACTLY IS THE OBSERVER?
goal: Test whether the witness has a fixed address.

steps.action: Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes.
Check behind the eyes, chest, head, and surrounding field.
Every found sensation is itself observed.
Rest with the inability to locate a final point.

win: ✓ The sentence stayed, but it stopped being the whole self.
supports: Exhale after “Rest Inability”; release extra load.
I can use “Check Behind” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Search Carefully → Check Behind → Observe Found → Rest Inability
safety:
PAUSE
Do not continue if location inquiry provokes feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.

steps.action: Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

win: ✓ Commentary moved to the cheap seat; the moment kept centre stage.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Unit”; mark the pause.
I can use “Centre Feedback” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Choose Skill → Centre Feedback → Demote Voice → Finish Unit
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if divided attention reduces accuracy or makes the activity unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
goal: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.

steps.action: Observe the same moment from three positions: body-centred, environment-centred, and whole-field.
Keep what each amplifies and hides.
Choose the position best suited to the upcoming task rather than declaring any one neutral.

win: ✓ Perspective became a tool for the task, not a claim of neutrality.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Position”; watch the thought.
I can use “Spot Amplifier” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Observe Moment → Spot Amplifier → Choose Position
safety:
PAUSE
Use a stable perspective when rotation increases disorientation or makes it harder to sense where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME
goal: What you notice exists briefly before concept files it.

steps.action: Look at or touch something ordinary.
Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.
Repeat with a sound.

win: ✓ A sound appeared before its label could grab it.
supports: Exhale after “Repeat Unnamed”; watch the thought.
I can use “Catch Bare” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Look Touch → Catch Bare → Don't Freeze → Repeat Unnamed
safety:
PAUSE
End if preidea-based attention feels unreal or confusing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE TODAY’S EMOTIONAL WEATHER
goal: You are the landscape experiencing weather, not the storm’s legal name.

steps.action: Imagine pressure zones, temperature, movement direction, visibility, and a likely prediction using colours or symbols.
Add one shelter and one safe travel route.
Revisit later to see what moved without forcing sunshine.

win: ✓ Today got a weather report, not a permanent identity.
supports: Exhale after “Check The Shift”; let feeling settle.
Compare “Map The Weather” with “Check The Shift”.
I can use “Add Shelter” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Map The Weather → Add Shelter → Check The Shift
safety:
PAUSE
Use direct crisis support when the weather includes dangerous impulses.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE INNER CAMERA
goal: Helplessness may be held in one visual angle.

steps.action: Adjust the internal scene’s distance, height, direction, and frame one at a time.
Test close, far, eye-level, above, behind, wide, and cropped.
Choose the angle that preserves facts while increasing present choice.

win: ✓ The facts stayed put while the camera found more choice.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Angle”; watch the thought.
I can use “Test Far” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Adjust → Test Far → Choose Angle
safety:
PAUSE
Traumatic visual work should be brief and supported when necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FOUR-CELL DECISION MATRIX
goal: Separate value from danger before emotion blends them.

steps.action: Score each option on value alignment, downside, reversibility, and learning.
Add a sentence explaining every score.
Compare patterns rather than relying on the total alone.
Favour the option with containable risk while important value is expressed.

win: ✓ Value and danger separated before either could rig the choice.
supports: Exhale after “Prefer Option”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Add Sentence” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Score Option → Add Sentence → Compare Patterns → Prefer Option
safety:
PAUSE
Use expert advice for high-stakes scoring assumptions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHICH REGRET ARE YOU AVOIDING?
goal: Regret has four species with different advice.

steps.action: For each option, estimate regret of action, inaction, delay, and self-betrayal.
Say the future scene behind the highest score.
Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values.

win: ✓ Regret split into types, and only one deserved to guide the choice.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Regret”; keep the compass.
I can use “Describe Future” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Estimate Regret → Describe Future → Ask Regret
safety:
PAUSE
Do not let imagined regret override present safety or evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE WHAT THE CHOICE WOULD ‘PROVE’
goal: Identity signalling can distort an otherwise practical decision.

steps.action: Name what each option would supposedly say about you—successful, loyal, brave, weak, ordinary.
Strike through those identity messages mentally.
Re-check only consequences, values, constraints, and evidence.
Notice whether the preferred option changes.

win: ✓ Identity stepped out of the voting booth; the practical choice became clearer.
supports: Exhale after “Notice Shift”; keep the compass.
I can use “Cross Out” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Say About → Cross Out → Check Again → Notice Shift
safety:
PAUSE
Identity and community may be legitimate values; distinguish them from performance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHOSE HANDWRITING IS ON THIS BELIEF?
goal: Inherited rules often feel like your own after the source fades.

steps.action: Name who modelled, rewarded, enforced, or normalised the belief.
Picture the original context and what compliance protected.
Now check if current-you endorses it under present values and data.

win: ✓ I found the old handwriting and decided whether the rule still deserved my signature.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Whether”; keep both sides.
I can use “Picture Original” before concluding.
formula_flow: Name Modelled → Picture Original → Ask Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid blaming cultures or individuals simplistically; systems transmit mixed messages.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.

steps.action: Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

win: ✓ The rule kept its ethical core and lost its fake universality.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Core”; keep both sides.
I can use “Change Context” before concluding.
formula_flow: State Rule → Change Context → Compare Effects → Keep Core
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the comparison turns into contempt for people or excuses unsafe or unlawful behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE COMPARISON DENOMINATOR
goal: A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.

steps.action: Name the group your mind selected.
Substitute a baseline matched on starting point, resources, time, responsibilities, and opportunity.
Compare progress with context included.
If no fair group exists, use your own prior trajectory.

win: ✓ The comparison group lost power; my own trajectory became the ruler.
supports: Exhale after “Group Exists”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Match Resources” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Name Mind → Match Resources → Compare Progress → Group Exists
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use context to deny areas where effort or repair is needed.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DO ONE GOOD THING WITH NO APPLAUSE BUTTON
goal: Values can survive the absence of approval.

steps.action: do a low-risk act you endorse and do it without announcing, checking reactions, or fishing for extra certainty.
Let the discomfort of no feedback rise and change.
Review the action by your values once it is done.

win: ✓ I did one good thing with no audience and it still counted.
supports: Exhale after “Review Quietly”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Let Discomfort” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Safe → Let Discomfort → Review Quietly
safety:
PAUSE
Do not conceal actions that require accountability, consent, or collaboration.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
